title: Review of c25's CIPS slow-product negative on fresh seed 5 and at dt/2: replicated, no division in any arm, packed enzyme cores keep their product
summary: labkit re-runs of the finding's world on seed 5 (128^2, t=3000) for five arms: starved fuel at Dp 1, 0.2 and 0.02, harder starvation at Dp 0.05, and Dp 0.2 at dt/2 (WORLD_P dt 0.05, 200 steps per frame; labkit labels the time 6000 but the physical time is 3000). Persistent splits are 0 in 4/5 arms; the harder-starvation arm (DF 0.02, y 5, Dp 0.05) records 1 persistent split against 30 merges, and its sheet shows a broken labyrinth fragmenting into a static emulsion of rods and droplets, not a body dividing. The core profiles reproduce c25's numbers almost exactly (Dp 1: e core/rim 0.92/0.63, p 0.109/0.089, F 0.169/0.247; Dp 0.2: 0.95/0.68, 0.132/0.109, 0.169/0.267), and dt/2 leaves them unchanged (0.95/0.68, 0.132/0.109). At Dp 0.02 only tiny droplets below 40 px remain (occupancy 0.02).

observations.finding: rerun/st2_dp005/sheet.png t=400-3000: labyrinth breaks into a static rod/droplet emulsion, no body divides; coreprof_seed5.txt: packed cores (e 0.92-0.95) with product at or above the rim in every arm with bodies

seeds_run.result: pass: 0 persistent splits in Dp 1, 0.2, 0.02 and dt/2; 1 persistent split vs 30 merges in DF 0.02/Dp 0.05 (rod fragmentation in a breaking labyrinth)

controls_run.dt: rerun/st_dp02_dthalf: world dt 0.1 -> 0.05 via WORLD_P, 200 steps per frame; the same counts and core profiles

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; no resolution variant; coreprof keeps bodies of >= 40 px, so the Dp 0.02 arm's tiny droplets are not profiled.
